subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Gravity Pulls Objects Down Toward Earth

items.prompt:
The force that pulls objects toward Earth is called
A) friction
B) gravity
C) magnetism
D) wind

Earth's gravity pulls objects
A) up
B) sideways
C) down toward the center of the Earth
D) in random directions
items.answer: C) down toward the center of the Earth

steps: Gravity always points toward Earth's center.

items.prompt:
If you drop a ball, it falls
A) up
B) down
C) sideways
D) it floats

steps: Gravity pulls the ball down to the ground.

items.prompt:
The measure of the pull of gravity on an object is its
A) color
B) weight
C) length
D) speed

steps: Weight measures the downward pull of gravity.

items.prompt:
A ball thrown straight up comes back down because
A) wind pushes it
B) gravity pulls it down toward Earth's center
C) it gets tired
D) magnets pull it
items.answer: B) gravity pulls it down toward Earth's center

steps: Gravity acts downward the whole time, so the ball returns.

items.prompt:
People in countries on opposite sides of the globe both stay on the ground because
A) gravity pulls each toward the center of the Earth
B) they wear heavy shoes
C) gravity only works in one country
D) the Earth is flat
items.answer: A) gravity pulls each toward the center of the Earth

steps: Down is toward the center for everyone on Earth.

items.prompt:
A feather and a rock are both released. The direction of gravity on them is
A) different for each
B) down toward Earth's center for both
C) up for the feather
D) sideways for the rock
items.answer: B) down toward Earth's center for both

steps: Gravity pulls all objects down toward the center, regardless of weight.

items.prompt:
A ball dropped from several floors of a tower always lands directly below. This supports the argument that gravity
A) points sideways
B) points straight down toward Earth's center
C) changes direction each floor
D) does not act on the ball
items.answer: B) points straight down toward Earth's center

steps: Landing directly below each time shows the force is straight down toward the center.
